# looking at dominant subjects
```{r}
H <- as.matrix(read.table('/Volumes/g_psyplafor_methlab$/Students/Katharina_Bremer/Output/Flica_Output/ABIDE/iterations1500/FSL_Format/150ica_wholesample/subjectCoursesOut.txt', header=FALSE)) #load in the subjects as component x subject 

# Dominance fraction for each component (as calculated by Llera)
subj_max <- apply(H^2, 1, max)
subj_total <- rowSums(H^2)
subj_dom <- subj_max / subj_total

dominant_subject <- apply(H^2, 1, which.max) #which subject dominates per component

# Summary table
dominance_df <- data.frame(
  Component = 1:(nrow(H)),
  DominantSubject = dominant_subject,
  DominanceFraction = subj_dom
)

print(dominance_df)

#using 0.02 as a threshold (which means max 2% of a component can be explained by one subject)
bad_components_0.02 <- dominance_df$Component[
  dominance_df$DominanceFraction > 0.02
]

bad_components_0.02_df <- data.frame(Component = bad_components_0.02)

bad_components_0.02_info <- dominance_df[dominance_df$Component %in% bad_components_0.02_df$Component,]

removesubs_002 <- unique(bad_components_0.02_info$DominantSubject)

removesubs_002
```

# removing the subjects with high subject dominance
```{r}

subj_list <-as.matrix(read.table('/Volumes/g_psyplafor_methlab$/Students/Katharina_Bremer/Input/ABIDEu30_final_subs.txt', header=FALSE)) 

subj_list_cleaned <- subj_list[-removesubs_002, ]

subj_list_cleaned <- as.matrix(subj_list_cleaned)

nrow(subj_list) - nrow(subj_list_cleaned) 


#check characterization
write.table(subj_list_cleaned, '/Volumes/g_psyplafor_methlab$/Students/Katharina_Bremer/Input/FSL_first_filter.txt', row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE, quote=FALSE)


#we need to take out stanford now (see: characterization script on FSL_first_filter. The amount of subjects in the sex x diagnosis groups is too small)

stanford <-as.matrix(read.table("/Volumes/g_psyplafor_methlab$/Students/Katharina_Bremer/Scripts/R Studio/Data/stanford_subs.txt", header=FALSE))

stanford_rows <- which(subj_list_cleaned %in% stanford)
subj_list_cleaned <- subj_list_cleaned[-stanford_rows, ]

subj_list_cleaned <- as.matrix(subj_list_cleaned)

#without stanford
write.table(subj_list_cleaned[,1], '/Volumes/g_psyplafor_methlab$/Students/Katharina_Bremer/Input/FSL_first_filter.txt',
            row.names = FALSE,
            col.names = FALSE,
            quote = FALSE)

```

# second filtering
```{r}
H <- as.matrix(read.table('/Volumes/g_psyplafor_methlab$/Students/Katharina_Bremer/Output/Flica_Output/ABIDE/iterations1500/FSL_Format/150ica_firstfilter/subjectCoursesOut.txt', header=FALSE)) #load in the subjects as component x subject 
dim(H)
# Dominance fraction for each component (as calculated by Llera)
subj_max <- apply(H^2, 1, max)
subj_total <- rowSums(H^2)
subj_dom <- subj_max / subj_total

dominant_subject <- apply(H^2, 1, which.max) #which subject dominates per component

# Summary table
dominance_df <- data.frame(
  Component = 1:(nrow(H)),
  DominantSubject = dominant_subject,
  DominanceFraction = subj_dom
)

print(dominance_df)

#using 0.02 as a threshold (which means max 2% of a component can be explained by one subject)
bad_components_0.02 <- dominance_df$Component[
  dominance_df$DominanceFraction > 0.02
]

bad_components_0.02_df <- data.frame(Component = bad_components_0.02)

bad_components_0.02_info <- dominance_df[dominance_df$Component %in% bad_components_0.02_df$Component,]

removesubs_002 <- unique(bad_components_0.02_info$DominantSubject)

removesubs_002

```

```{r}

subj_list <-as.matrix(read.table('/Volumes/g_psyplafor_methlab$/Students/Katharina_Bremer/Input/FSL_first_filter.txt', header=FALSE)) 
ncol(H) == nrow(subj_list) #this is why we can remove by index

subj_list_cleaned <- subj_list[-removesubs_002, ]

subj_list_cleaned <- as.matrix(subj_list_cleaned)

nrow(subj_list) - nrow(subj_list_cleaned) 


#check characterization
write.table(subj_list_cleaned, '/Volumes/g_psyplafor_methlab$/Students/Katharina_Bremer/Input/FSL_second_filter.txt', row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE, quote=FALSE)
```
